answer: Think of the agent economy as a tended garden: every identity must plant a costly, non-transferable stake — a bond as hard and verifiable as onyx — before it can transact. Creating a thousand fake agents then means locking a thousand bonds, so a Sybil flood costs as much as the identities it fakes. Misbehavior burns the stake like an ember consuming its fuel, and honest agents keep their bond plus fees. The defense works because the price of one fake identity stays high while the price of one honest identity stays low.
